newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish paint producer Bayrakli to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish paint producer Bayrakli to float shares.

text.p: Turkish paint and varnish producer Bayrakl Boya ve Vernik Sanayii A.S. said it would float 160 billion lira nominal-valued new shares in a public offer between May 30 and June 2.
The fixed price would be 7,500 lira for each 1,000 lira nominal valued share in the offer managed by Global Securities, the company said in a statement.
The consortium includes Yap Kredi Investment, Ekinciler Investment, Strateji Securities, Yasar Investment, Acar Securities, Es Securities, K Investment and Kent Investment.

The company will waive 160 billion lira of pre-emptive rights to sell them to the public when raising its capital to 460 billion lira from current 300 billion lira. 128 billion lira of the total offer will be allocated to foreign investors.
Bayrakl Boya, owned by Turkey's Aegean-based food and paint group Yasar Holding, specialises in furniture painting where it holds a 21 percent market share.
Its domestic market shares are 29 percent in industrial paints, 18 percent in polyester resin and five percent in construction paints.
The company plans to raise overall output capacity to 75,000 tonnes per year from 35,000 tonnes when a new factory becomes operational in October 1997.
It has a distribution network of 55 wholesalers and 400 retailers in Turkey. It also has direct sales to 240 industrial plants.
Bayrakli Boya raised its 1996 net profits to 148 billion lira and net sales to 3.83 trillion lira in 1996, up from 60.6 billion and 2.03 trillion lira in 1995.
